description: This topic covers the general characteristics of the animal kingdom and the main invertebrate phyla, including their key features, examples, and economic or medical importance.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a general characteristic of all members of the kingdom Animalia?

options.text: They make their own food by photosynthesis
They are eukaryotic, multicellular and heterotrophic
They all have a rigid cellulose cell wall
They are all single-celled and fixed in one place

mcq.explanation: Animals are eukaryotic, multicellular organisms that feed on other organisms (heterotrophic), lack a cell wall, and are usually able to move.

mcq.questionText: Why are animals described as heterotrophic?

options.text: They obtain food by feeding on other organisms
They absorb minerals directly from soil
They do not need food at all

mcq.explanation: Heterotrophic means an organism cannot make its own food and must obtain organic food by eating other living or dead organisms.

mcq.questionText: To which phylum does a sponge belong?
mcq.explanation: Sponges belong to the phylum Porifera. Their bodies have many tiny pores through which water enters to bring food.

mcq.questionText: Hydra, jellyfish and corals all belong to the phylum:
mcq.explanation: Hydra, jellyfish and corals are coelenterates (cnidarians). They have stinging cells and a body with radial symmetry.

mcq.questionText: Which structures do cnidarians such as Hydra use to capture prey and for defence?
mcq.explanation: Cnidarians have special stinging cells called cnidocytes (nematocysts) on their tentacles, used to paralyse prey and for defence.

mcq.questionText: A tapeworm and planaria are examples of organisms in the phylum:
mcq.explanation: Tapeworms and planaria are flatworms belonging to the phylum Platyhelminthes, which have flattened bodies; many are parasitic.

mcq.questionText: Ascaris and hookworm are classified under which phylum?
mcq.explanation: Ascaris and hookworm are roundworms in the phylum Nematoda. They have long, cylindrical, unsegmented bodies and several are human parasites.

mcq.questionText: What is a key feature that distinguishes annelids such as the earthworm from roundworms?

options.text: Their bodies are flat and ribbon-like
Their bodies are divided into many rings or segments
They have a hard external shell

mcq.explanation: Annelids are segmented worms; their bodies are divided into many ring-like segments. Earthworms and leeches are common examples.

mcq.questionText: Snails, slugs and octopuses are members of the phylum:
mcq.explanation: Molluscs have soft bodies that are often protected by a hard shell. Snails, slugs and octopuses are all molluscs.

mcq.questionText: Which phylum is the largest group in the animal kingdom and includes insects, spiders and crabs?
mcq.explanation: Arthropoda is the largest animal phylum. Its members have jointed legs and a hard exoskeleton, and include insects, arachnids, crustaceans and myriapods.

mcq.questionText: Which two features are characteristic of all arthropods?

options.text: A soft body and a coiled shell

mcq.explanation: All arthropods have jointed appendages (legs) and a hard outer exoskeleton made mainly of chitin, which they shed as they grow.

mcq.questionText: Starfish and sea urchins belong to the phylum Echinodermata, which is characterised by:

options.text: Many pores in the body wall

mcq.explanation: Echinoderms have a spiny skin and radial symmetry (body parts arranged around a central point). They live in the sea and include starfish and sea urchins.

mcq.questionText: Which arthropod group includes spiders, scorpions and ticks, typically having eight legs?
mcq.explanation: Arachnids, such as spiders, scorpions and ticks, are arthropods that usually have eight legs and a body divided into two main regions.

mcq.questionText: Which of these invertebrates is most directly important to humans as a parasite that causes disease?
mcq.explanation: The tapeworm is a parasitic flatworm that lives in the human intestine and causes disease by taking digested food, leading to weakness and malnutrition.

mcq.questionText: Which statement correctly describes the economic importance of insects?

options.text: Insects are only harmful and have no useful role
Some insects are crop pests while others act as pollinators
All insects produce shells used in industry
Insects cannot transmit diseases to humans

mcq.explanation: Insects have both harmful and useful roles: some, like locusts, destroy crops, while others, like bees, pollinate flowers and produce honey.

fib.questionText: Animals are multicellular organisms that obtain food by feeding on others, so they are described as _____.
fib.explanation: Heterotrophic organisms cannot make their own food and must eat other organisms.

fib.questionText: Unlike plant cells, animal cells do not have a _____.
fib.explanation: Animal cells lack a cell wall; they are surrounded only by a cell membrane, which allows movement and flexibility.

fib.questionText: Sponges belong to the phylum _____, whose members have many pores in their body wall.
fib.explanation: Porifera means pore-bearers; water enters through pores carrying food and oxygen.

fib.questionText: Cnidarians such as Hydra use special _____ cells on their tentacles to capture prey.
fib.explanation: Stinging cells (cnidocytes or nematocysts) paralyse prey and are used for defence.

fib.questionText: Flatworms such as the tapeworm and planaria belong to the phylum _____.
fib.explanation: Platyhelminthes are flatworms with flattened bodies; many of them are parasitic.

fib.questionText: Roundworms such as Ascaris and hookworm belong to the phylum _____.
fib.explanation: Nematoda are roundworms with long cylindrical unsegmented bodies; some are human parasites.

fib.questionText: The earthworm and the leech are examples of segmented worms in the phylum _____.
fib.explanation: Annelids have bodies divided into many ring-like segments.

fib.questionText: Animals with soft bodies that are often protected by a shell, such as snails, belong to the phylum _____.
fib.explanation: Molluscs have soft bodies usually covered by a hard shell; examples include snails, slugs and octopuses.

fib.questionText: The largest phylum in the animal kingdom, whose members have jointed legs and an exoskeleton, is _____.
fib.explanation: Arthropoda is the largest animal phylum and includes insects, arachnids, crustaceans and myriapods.

fib.questionText: Starfish and sea urchins have a spiny skin and _____ symmetry, where body parts are arranged around a central point.
fib.explanation: Echinoderms show radial symmetry, with their body parts arranged around a central axis.

tf.questionText: All animals are able to make their own food through photosynthesis.
tf.explanation: Animals are heterotrophic; they cannot photosynthesise and must feed on other organisms.

tf.questionText: Invertebrates are animals that do not have a backbone.
tf.explanation: Invertebrates lack a vertebral column (backbone); all the phyla in this topic are invertebrates.

tf.questionText: Sponges (Porifera) have true tissues and organs like complex animals.
tf.explanation: Sponges are simple animals without true tissues or organs; they filter food from water passing through their pores.

tf.questionText: Jellyfish and corals possess stinging cells used to capture prey.
tf.explanation: Like all cnidarians, jellyfish and corals have stinging cells (cnidocytes) on their tentacles.

tf.questionText: All members of the phylum Platyhelminthes are free-living and harmless.
tf.explanation: Many flatworms, such as tapeworms and flukes, are parasites that cause disease, although some like planaria are free-living.

tf.questionText: The body of an annelid is divided into many segments.
tf.explanation: Annelids are segmented worms; the earthworm's body is clearly divided into ring-like segments.

tf.questionText: An octopus is a mollusc even though it does not have an external shell.
tf.explanation: The octopus is a mollusc with a soft body; its shell is reduced or absent, but it shares other molluscan features.

tf.questionText: Arthropods grow continuously without ever shedding their exoskeleton.
tf.explanation: Because the exoskeleton is hard and cannot stretch, arthropods must moult (shed) it to grow.

tf.questionText: Echinoderms such as starfish live mainly in the sea.
tf.explanation: Echinoderms are marine animals; examples include starfish and sea urchins found in the ocean.

tf.questionText: Bees are economically important because they pollinate flowers and produce honey.
tf.explanation: Bees are useful insects: they pollinate many crops and produce honey and beeswax.

summary.questionText: State four general characteristics of the kingdom Animalia.
summary.correctAnswer: They are eukaryotic, multicellular, heterotrophic, lack a cell wall and are usually able to move.
summary.explanation: These features distinguish animals from plants, fungi and other kingdoms.

summary.correctAnswer: An animal that does not have a backbone (vertebral column).
summary.explanation: All the phyla studied in this topic, such as Porifera and Arthropoda, are invertebrates.

summary.questionText: Describe the main feature of the phylum Porifera.
summary.correctAnswer: Sponges have bodies with many pores through which water passes to bring food and oxygen.
summary.explanation: The pores give the phylum its name (Porifera = pore-bearers).

summary.questionText: Give two examples of cnidarians and state one special structure they all have.
summary.correctAnswer: Examples: Hydra, jellyfish or corals; they all have stinging cells.
summary.explanation: Cnidarians use stinging cells on their tentacles to capture prey and defend themselves.

summary.questionText: How do flatworms (Platyhelminthes) differ in body shape from roundworms (Nematoda)?
summary.correctAnswer: Flatworms have flat, ribbon-like bodies while roundworms have round, cylindrical bodies.
summary.explanation: Body shape is a simple way to tell these two worm phyla apart.

summary.questionText: Name the phylum of segmented worms and give two examples.
summary.correctAnswer: Annelida; examples are the earthworm and the leech.
summary.explanation: Annelids have bodies divided into many rings or segments.

summary.questionText: What are the main characteristics of molluscs?
summary.correctAnswer: They have soft bodies that are often protected by a hard shell.
summary.explanation: Examples include snails, slugs and octopuses.

summary.questionText: List the four main groups of arthropods.
summary.explanation: All arthropods share jointed legs and an exoskeleton, but they are divided into these groups.

summary.questionText: Why is the phylum Arthropoda considered the most successful animal group?
summary.correctAnswer: It is the largest phylum with the greatest number of species, found in nearly all habitats; the exoskeleton and jointed legs help survival.
summary.explanation: Their hard exoskeleton gives protection and support, and jointed legs allow varied movement.

summary.questionText: Give one harmful and one useful example of the importance of invertebrates to humans.
summary.correctAnswer: Harmful: parasitic worms such as tapeworm or hookworm cause disease; Useful: bees pollinate crops and make honey.
summary.explanation: Invertebrates affect human life both negatively (parasites and pests) and positively (pollination and food).

hoq.questionText: A student finds a small worm in soil. Its body is long, soft and clearly divided into many ring-like segments, and it helps mix the soil. To which phylum does it most likely belong?
hoq.explanation: A segmented soil worm that mixes soil is an earthworm, a member of the phylum Annelida; segmentation is the key clue.

hoq.questionText: A patient is found to be weak, losing weight and has flat, ribbon-like worm segments in the stool after eating undercooked meat. Which invertebrate is most likely the cause?
hoq.explanation: Flat, ribbon-like segments and infection from undercooked meat point to a tapeworm, a parasitic flatworm in the intestine.

hoq.questionText: A new sea animal is discovered with a hard spiny skin, no backbone, body parts arranged around a central point (radial symmetry), and it moves using tiny tube feet. It should be classified in which phylum?
hoq.explanation: Spiny skin, radial symmetry and tube feet are defining features of echinoderms such as starfish and sea urchins.
